ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: In the figure there is a square with a black outer frame, and inside is a gray cross-shaped dodecagon. The gray dodecagon is composed of 12 slanted sides that look congruent, and each slanted side is in a 45° direction relative to the horizontal side or vertical side of the square. Observing according to the direction in the figure, the positions where the vertices of the gray figure touch the boundary of the square make the length of one side of the square correspond to the horizontal or vertical projections of 4 such 45° slanted sides. Then reason: The dodecagon is equilateral, and its perimeter is 36 cm, so each side length is 36/12 = 3 cm. Each slanted side makes 45° with the horizontal/vertical direction, therefore the horizontal or vertical projection of one side is 3/√2 cm. The side length of the square equals 4 such projections, so the side length is 4 · 3/√2 = 12/√2 = 6√2 cm. The area of the square is (6√2)^2 = 72 cm².

method.method_draft: Use the diagram in its displayed orientation. From the image, note that the gray dodecagon has 12 congruent slanted sides, each at 45 degrees to the horizontal/vertical sides of the surrounding square, and its vertices lie so that one side of the square is divided into four equal horizontal projection intervals. From the text, the dodecagon perimeter is 36 cm and it is equilateral, so each dodecagon side has length 36/12 = 3 cm. For a 45-45-90 step, the horizontal or vertical projection of one gray side is 3/sqrt(2). The side length of the black square is four such projections: 4(3/sqrt(2)) = 6sqrt(2). Therefore the square area is (6sqrt(2))^2 = 72.

method.method_draft: Mentally rotate the gray dodecagon by 45 degrees. From the image and the phrase right-angled cross-shaped dodecagon, recognize it as the boundary of a Greek cross made from five congruent squares. The 12 boundary segments of that cross all have the same length, so if the dodecagon perimeter is 36 cm, the side length of each small square in the Greek cross is 36/12 = 3 cm. In the unrotated Greek cross, the distance from one extreme arm tip to the opposite extreme arm tip in a diagonal direction equals four small-square side lengths, so after rotating back this is the diagonal of the enclosing square: 4·3 = 12 cm. A square with diagonal 12 has area 12^2/2 = 72.
